recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change ElementDefinition.constraint.human to markdown unless FHIR-I reopens the prior no-core-change decision; use the rendering-markdown extension for marked-up constraint messages.
issue_request: FHIR-28141 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. The Jira description asked to change ElementDefinition.constraint.requirements to markdown, the reporter comment said they meant constraint.human, and the recorded resolution named constraint.human, binding.description, and mapping.comment.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged implementation commit a74d790b4480099fb9d8b68ad2df3bef4844d99b changed source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml so constraint.requirements, binding.description, and mapping.comment are markdown; it left constraint.human as string.
additional_context: FHIR-25392 had already rejected changing ElementDefinition.constraint.human to markdown and recommended using the rendering-markdown extension. FHIR-I minutes on 2022-08-29 explicitly recorded the FHIR-25392/FHIR-28141 conflict, concluded FHIR-28141 had a typo in the resolution, and said both tickets were already applied correctly. The matching Zulip thread records Grahame Grieve saying FHIR-28141 should read as changing constraint.requirements, binding.description, and mapping.comment.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Current build-scoped source has ElementDefinition.constraint.requirements, ElementDefinition.binding.description, and ElementDefinition.mapping.comment as markdown, and ElementDefinition.constraint.human as string, which matches the later clarified interpretation.

related_jiras.note: Published/Not Persuasive with Modification decision rejected making ElementDefinition.constraint.human markdown and supports reading FHIR-28141 as applying to constraint.requirements instead.

evidence_items.learned: This is the decisive WG context that the current source should not be changed to make constraint.human markdown.
